elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Revised 13.2: "Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement at any time, for any reasons by giving thirty (30) days advance written notice to Array" — Ono (Customer) holds an unconditional convenience right; no Order Forms exist in this license agreement structure.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "by giving thirty (30) days advance written notice to Array" — the redacted [ * ] notice period is replaced with a fixed 30 days' written notice. The retained requirement that notice be accompanied by a rationale is pre-existing favourable-neutral language and does not condition the right.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "Array shall refund to Ono, on a pro rata basis, any fees prepaid by Ono for the period after the effective date of such termination." — express pro rata basis stated, not merely a post-termination-period refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Article 13 as cited affords Array only for-cause exits (13.3 material breach, 13.4 bankruptcy); 13.1 runs to expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term "unless terminated earlier pursuant to this Article 13". No Array convenience right appears in the cited or rendered text, so the element is already satisfied without edit. Cannot fully verify unseen 13.3-13.5 text, but the cited record shows no Vendor at-will exit.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Notice is fixed at thirty (30) days, which is shorter than (and better than) the 60-90 day fallback band; the fallback band is therefore not literally met.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee, penalty, or contingent payment mechanic is imposed on Ono in revised 13.2; the condition does not apply, so the cap requirement is satisfied vacuously.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Array has no convenience termination right at all under Article 13 as rendered, which is stricter than the fallback limitation; condition inapplicable.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Array holds no convenience termination right, so no notice floor is engaged; condition inapplicable.

reasons: All four preferred elements are met in the rendered operative language: the delayed commencement tied to the later of two redacted First Commercial Sale periods is deleted so the right is exercisable 'at any time', the redacted notice period is fixed at thirty (30) days' advance written notice, an express pro rata refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period is added, and Array retains no convenience exit under Article 13.

The finding is correctly classified as a deviation: pre-redline, Ono had no convenience right for a multi-year stretch of a term running to expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term, which is walk-away territory under the rule ('No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term'), and the notice period was redacted rather than fixed.

Minimality holds. The edit touches only Section 13.2, retains the favourable existing 'for any reasons' language and the pre-existing rationale-with-notice mechanic, and adds no survival tail, at-own-expense language, procedures, or extras. The model language's 'in whole or in part' and 'or any Order Form' were correctly omitted because there is no Order Form or partial-termination structure in this license agreement, consistent with the T4C surplus guidance. Section 13.1 is quoted only as evidence of the already-met Vendor element and is left unamended.

Intent is preserved. Section 13.1's term, expiry, post-expiry perpetual license, trademark and domain name mechanics survive unchanged; the 'unless terminated earlier pursuant to this Article 13' hook continues to operate; no undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence is created. Array's for-cause exits (13.3, 13.4) and the Section 8.2 competing-product trigger are untouched.

The deterministic check 'Customer convenience termination present: false' is a false negative on inspection: revised 13.2 is captioned 'Termination by Ono without Cause' and grants Ono the right to terminate 'at any time, for any reasons', which is an unconditional Customer election and therefore a convenience right under the stated rule boundary. The substance overrides the regex miss.

The fallback level is not complete solely because the notice period is 30 days rather than 60-90 days; this is a better-than-fallback outcome and does not affect position completeness, which is achieved at the preferred level.

One residual point for the drafter to confirm (not a defect in the rendered text): the preferred Vendor element relies on Article 13.3-13.5 and Section 8.2 containing no Array at-will exit. That was verified against the finding rationale but the full text of those subsections was not supplied; confirm before sending that no Array convenience right survives elsewhere in Article 13.
